question.worked_solution:
First, we convert $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians to an equivalent measure in degrees. This gives

$$
(\frac{\pi }{4})(\frac{{180}^{∘}}{\pi })=\frac{{180}^{∘}}{4}={45}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, since we know that $\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
